messages.author: 890c64c56aea6f77
messages.subject: Default graphics devices on shinyapps.io
parts:
My app displays an interactive plot via renderUI. The code that creates the interactive plot generates and prints a ggplot object to a temporary pdf file as a byproduct. This seems to fail on shinyapps.io but I cannot reproduce the error locally. 

Is there something I am missing about how graphics devices work on shinyapps? I assumed that the pdf() function with dev.off() would work on any R installation. The error I am getting is 

error in evaluating the argument 'group' in selecting a method for function 'devStartGroup': Error in if (isUTF8) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed Calls: devGrob ... devGrob.viewport -> getID -> prefixName -> paste0 -> escapeSelector

The app is hosted here: https://sachsmc.shinyapps.io/plotROC/
And the code can be seen here: https://github.com/sachsmc/plotROC/tree/master/inst/shinyApp

Any insight would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 890c64c56aea6f77
messages.subject: Re: Default graphics devices on shinyapps.io
parts:
Here's a minimal example: 


shinyApp(
   ui = shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  
  htmlOutput("test")
  
  )), 

     server = shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  library(shiny)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(grid)
  library(gridSVG)
  
  
  output$test <- renderUI({
  
      p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = hp)) + geom_point(size = 5) + 
        scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-50, 500)) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 50))
      
      pdf(file = tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
      print(p)
      
      grid.force()
   
      tmpFile <- tempfile()
      svgString <- gridSVG::grid.export(name = tmpFile, prefix = "cars")$svg
      svgString <- paste(readLines(tmpFile, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
      dev.off()
      
      HTML(svgString)
      
  })
  
}))

         server = shinyServer(function(input, output) {
           output$mess <- renderPrint({ localeToCharset() })

           ))

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: Default graphics devices on shinyapps.io
parts:
I think this is probably a bug in R, or at least a incompatibility with recent versions of Ubuntu. ShinyApps runs uses C.UTF-8 locale, which R doesn't recognize as being UTF-8 encoded. 

Perhaps this a workaround:

localeToCharset <- function() { "UTF-8" }
